newsitem.title: USA: Argentine Congress to OK tax plan by Oct - Corach.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Congress to OK tax plan by Oct - Corach.

text.p: The Argentine Congress will approve the government's austerity measures by October amid strong support from the ruling Peronist party, an administration official said Wednesday.
Argentina's Interior Minister Carlos Corach said here that Congress will pass the tax program, unveiled last month by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, with minimal changes.

"I am sure that all the Peronist party -- 99 percent of the Peronist party -- is behind the President's austerity program," Corach said after addressing the Americas Society. "The tax program will be approved by October by both chambers."
Corach said he had no doubt that Congress would not signifcantly water down the measures. "We believe that the main line of the tax program will be approved, maybe with some little changes."
The Chamber of Deputies removed at the committee stage extensions of value added tax and a rise in women's retirement age to 65 from 60.
"The taxes now in Congress will be approved, maybe with some changes in the secondary aspects," Corach said. The Chamber will debate the measures today.

The minister added that the plan would not affect Argentine production or stability. "I really believe the impact on the whole economy will not be very important," he said, adding that the government was addressing an important challenge to fight tax evasion.
He said that the administration was commited to fiscal austerity, but had little fat to cut from its federal budget.
"We are not spending an amount of money from which we can make spectacular reductions," he said.
The Congress would also approve labor reform legislation within the next month-and-a-half, he said.
The Peronists would not veer from the commitment to fiscal discipline despite slumping support for President Carlos Menem, the minister said.
"To win elections, we must win as we won in previous national elections, and not by softening our policies," he added.
He dismissed a press account last week that Menem would attempt to run for a third term of office.
"This is not true," he said of the report. "You need to reform the constitution and you know how difficult that is."

He also rejected a published report that former economic advisor Guillermo Calvo called for an "indirect" devaluation through lifting Mercosur external tarriffs. "We will not devalue in any way," Corach said.
